oneLiner: 不是懒，是「现在的情绪」压过了「未来的自己」。
oneLinerEn: Not laziness—present feelings override the future self.
detail: 为什么：面对厌恶任务，大脑立刻想逃，短期缓解强化了拖延。怎么办：把任务拆小到「5 分钟能开始」；用「先做完再奖励」替代「先玩再忙」；接受不完美初稿。
detailEn: Why: facing a dreaded task, the brain flees for quick relief, reinforcing the habit. What helps: shrink tasks to 'start in 5 min'; reward after, not before; accept an imperfect first draft.

sources.label: 《拖延心理学》
sources.labelEn: Steel, Procrastination: Why You Do It, What to Do About It

oneLiner: 一天做太多选择，后面就越随便或越冲动。
oneLinerEn: Too many choices in a day makes later ones careless or impulsive.
detail: 表现：晚饭点不动、购物乱买、对家人没耐心。为什么：自控是有限资源，会耗尽。怎么办：把重要决定放上午；固定琐碎选择（同款衣/食）；留出「不做决定」的时段。
detailEn: How it shows: can't pick dinner, impulse buys, short temper. Why: self-control is a limited, depletable resource. What helps: decide big things in the morning; automate small choices; schedule decision-free time.

sources.label: Baumeister et al. (1998)

oneLiner: 刷得越久越空：比较和算法在悄悄消耗你。
oneLinerEn: More scrolling, more hollow: comparison and algorithms drain you.
detail: 机制：别人的精选人生引发上行比较，多巴胺循环让人停不下。怎么办：关推送、设时段；用「主动创作」替代「被动刷」；睡前一小时不碰屏幕。
detailEn: Mechanism: others' highlights trigger upward comparison; dopamine loops keep you in. What helps: kill notifications, set time windows; create instead of scroll; no screens an hour before bed.

sources.label: Twenge (2017)

oneLiner: 亲密里的反应，常是童年依恋模式的重演。
oneLinerEn: How we react in love often replays childhood attachment.
detail: 三种模式：安全型（可依赖也可独处）、焦虑型（怕被弃、需确认）、回避型（疏离、怕被缠）。怎么办：看清自己的模式，用「直接表达需求」替代试探；对方模式不同别急于贴标签。
detailEn: Three patterns: secure (depend and be alone), anxious (fear abandonment, need reassurance), avoidant (distant, fear engulfment). What helps: name your pattern; say needs plainly instead of testing; don't rush to label the other.

sources.label: Bowlby (1969)

oneLiner: 不是累了睡一觉就好，是长期失控与耗竭。
oneLinerEn: Not fixed by sleep—chronic depletion from loss of control.
detail: 三征兆：情绪耗竭、对工作疏离、效能感下降。为什么：资源长期小于需求、缺乏自主。怎么办：找回小块掌控感（自己排优先级）；设边界；必要时谈工作量调整。本站不提供诊断。
detailEn: Three signs: exhaustion, detachment, low efficacy. Why: demand outruns resources, little autonomy. What helps: reclaim small control (set your own priorities); set boundaries; discuss load if needed. Not a diagnosis here.

sources.label: Maslach (1981)

oneLiner: 夸「努力」比夸「聪明」更能扛挫折。
oneLinerEn: Praising effort beats praising smarts for resilience.
detail: 机制：夸天赋让人怕失败、回避难事；夸努力让人把困难当练习（成长型思维）。怎么办：描述具体行为（「你刚才很专注」），少贴「聪明/笨」标签。
detailEn: Mechanism: praising talent breeds fear of failure; praising effort treats hard tasks as practice (growth mindset). What helps: name the behavior ('you stayed focused'), avoid 'smart/dumb' labels.

sources.label: Dweck (2006)

oneLiner: 睡好觉，大脑才把白天的信息「归档」。
oneLinerEn: In sleep, the brain files away the day's information.
detail: 机制：深睡期巩固记忆、清理代谢废物；缺睡则学不牢、情绪更脆。怎么办：固定作息、睡前降蓝光；考前别熬夜——睡眠本身就在复习。
detailEn: Mechanism: deep sleep consolidates memory and clears waste; lack of it weakens learning and frays mood. What helps: regular sleep, less screen light; don't pull all-nighters—sleep is review.

sources.label: Walker (2017)

oneLiner: 习惯由「线索→行为→奖赏」自动循环，改习惯从改线索开始。
oneLinerEn: A habit is a cue→routine→reward loop; change it by altering the cue.
detail: 机制：重复使行为从有意识控制转入基底神经节的自动程序，一遇线索就触发。怎么办：想养成好习惯，把线索醒目化、行为拆小（两分钟版）、即时奖励；想戒除，隐藏或替换线索、保留旧奖赏但换新行为。环境设计往往比意志力更省力。
detailEn: Mechanism: repetition moves a behavior from deliberate control to automatic basal-ganglia routines fired by cues. To build a habit, make cues visible, shrink the action (a 2-minute version) and reward it now; to break one, hide or swap the cue and keep the reward but change the routine. Designing the environment beats raw willpower.

sources.label: Duhigg (2012)《习惯的力量》
sources.labelEn: Duhigg (2012), The Power of Habit

oneLiner: 分次复习 + 主动默写回想，远比反复重读更记得住。
oneLinerEn: Spaced review plus active recall beats rereading for lasting memory.
detail: 机制：间隔克服遗忘曲线、提取（自测）比重读更能强化痕迹，也暴露盲点。怎么办：用抽卡/闪卡隔几天自测、做习题而非反复看课本；宁可当下想得费力，也好过虚假的熟练感。这是证据最硬的学习法之一。
detailEn: Mechanism: spacing counters the forgetting curve, and retrieval (self-testing) strengthens traces and exposes gaps better than rereading. Use flashcards with gaps of days, do practice problems rather than re-read; prefer effortful recall over a false sense of fluency. This is among the best-evidenced study methods.

sources.label: Roediger & Karpicke (2006)

oneLiner: 见面几秒就形成的判断会晕轮式地拉高对其他特质的评价。
oneLinerEn: Snap judgments formed in seconds spill over, inflating ratings of other traits.
detail: 机制：首因效应与晕轮效应让一个突出优点（外貌、流利）污染整体判断。怎么办：招聘、交友、评审时先定好标准、分开逐项打分、延迟综合判断；意识到“看顺眼”不等于“有能力”，主动寻找反证。
detailEn: Mechanism: primacy and the halo effect let one salient trait (looks, fluency) color the whole judgment. In hiring, dating and review, set criteria first, score traits separately and defer a global call; remember 'likable' is not 'competent' and actively seek disconfirming evidence.

sources.label: Thorndike (1920) 晕轮效应
sources.labelEn: Thorndike (1920), A Constant Error in Psychological Ratings

oneLiner: 说出「我现在很焦虑」本身就能稍稍调低情绪的强度。
oneLinerEn: Saying 'I feel anxious' itself dials down the emotion's intensity.
detail: 机制：用词标注情绪会增强前额叶对杏仁核的抑制，把“被情绪淹没”转为“观察情绪”。怎么办：情绪上来时先具体命名（生气/失望/羡慕）、写在纸上；配合呼吸与认知重评。“说出来”不是软弱，而是有效的自我调节。
detailEn: Mechanism: labeling an emotion boosts prefrontal inhibition of the amygdala, shifting you from being flooded to observing. When feelings rise, name them specifically (angry/disappointed/envious), put them on paper, pair with breath and reappraisal. 'Saying it' is not weakness but effective regulation.

sources.label: Lieberman (2007) 情绪标注的神经机制
sources.labelEn: Lieberman (2007), Putting Feelings into Words

oneLiner: 焦虑占用了工作记忆，让人“明明会却考砸”。
oneLinerEn: Anxiety hogs working memory, so what you knew 'slips' under pressure.
detail: 机制：担忧念头与抑制压力占用工作记忆，剩下给题目的容量减少。怎么办：考前模拟真实环境、熟练到自动；开考前写下担忧（表达性写作）以卸下载荷；把“紧张”重评为“兴奋/准备就绪”。重点不是消除焦虑，而是不让它吃掉思考资源。
detailEn: Mechanism: worry and pressure-suppression consume working memory, leaving less for the items. Simulate real conditions, overlearn to automaticity, jot worries down before starting (expressive writing) to unload them, and reappraise 'nervous' as 'excited/ready'. The goal is not zero anxiety but keeping it from eating your thinking resources.

sources.label: Beilock (2010)《你的头脑如何欺骗你》
sources.labelEn: Beilock (2010), Choke

term: 选择越多反而越难抉择
oneLiner: 选项一多，反悔成本、比较负担与「错过更好」的担忧齐升，人反而更容易焦虑、拖延甚至弃选。
oneLinerEn: As options multiply, so do the cost of switching, the burden of comparing and fear of missing a better one—leaving people more anxious, stalled, or ready to opt out.
detail: 超市里 24 种果酱的试吃台，远不如 6 种的那张促成更多购买——这就是「选择过载」的经典演示。选项一多，人要为比较付出更多认知成本，还要承担「万一错过更优」的预期后悔；当决定本身并不那么重要时，最大化者总想穷尽所有选项，于是越挑越累。破解之道是主动设限：先定「够好即可」的标准与可接受的少数几个候选，把「要不要再多看一个」的诱惑挡在框架之外。
detailEn: A tasting table of 24 jams closes far fewer sales than one with 6—this is the classic demonstration of choice overload. More options raise the cognitive cost of comparing and the anticipated regret of missing a better pick; when the choice hardly matters, maximizers still want to survey everything and grow weary picking. The fix is to set limits on purpose: define a 'good enough' bar and a shortlist, and shut the 'should I look at one more' temptation outside your frame.

sources.label: Iyengar & Lepper (2000), When Choice Is Demotivating

oneLiner: 所谓多任务，其实是在任务间快速来回切换，每次切换都要「重新加载」——越忙越低效、还更易出错。
oneLinerEn: 'Multitasking' is really rapid task-switching; each switch forces a mental reload—busier yet less efficient, and more error-prone.
detail: 大脑并不真的并行处理两件需要注意的事，而是像在不同标签页间反复刷新。每次切换都带来「切换成本」：先放下旧任务的语境、再重建新任务的规则，误差也随之抬头。写论文时回消息、开会时改邮件，看似高效，实则以更浅的专注换更多的返工。频繁切换还会训练出「等不住」的注意习惯。真正省力的做法是批次化：一次只给一类任务一段不被打断的时间，把切换次数压到最低。
detailEn: The brain doesn't truly run two attention-requiring tasks at once; it refreshes between them like switching browser tabs. Each switch carries a switching cost—dropping the old context, rebuilding the new task's rules—and errors creep in. Answering messages while writing, editing email during a meeting looks productive but trades deeper focus for more rework. Frequent switching also trains a restless attention. The effort-saving move is batching: give one class of task an uninterrupted block and keep switches to a minimum.

sources.label: Monsell (2003), Task Switching

oneLiner: 被无视、被排挤会激活与躯体疼痛相近的脑区——社会性痛是真实的痛。
oneLinerEn: Being ignored or excluded recruits brain regions near physical pain—social hurt is real hurt.
detail: 进化把人绑在群体上：在远古，被部落排斥几乎等于判死刑，于是大脑演化出对「归属受威胁」的强烈警报，其神经影像与被烫到时重叠。哪怕只是网络传球游戏里被两人有意不传（Cyberball），被试也会报告情绪低落，且越是长期被冷暴力，越先伤及「归属感、控制感、自尊、存在意义」这四种基本需要。理解这一点，不是为了沉溺受害感，而是明白：对被排挤者轻说「别那么敏感」既不属实，也毫无安慰之效；而重建联结、寻找新群体，是缓解这种痛的正路。
detailEn: Evolution bound humans to the group: in deep antiquity exile from the tribe was near a death sentence, so the brain grew a strong alarm for threatened belonging, overlapping on imaging with the pain of a burn. Even being deliberately left out of an online ball-toss game (Cyberball) lowers mood, and prolonged cold-shouldering first strikes four basic needs—belonging, control, self-esteem and meaningful existence. Knowing this isn't to wallow in victimhood but to see that telling the excluded 'don't be so sensitive' is both inaccurate and no comfort; rebuilding connection and finding a new group is the true path through the pain.

sources.label: Williams (2007), Ostracism: The Power of Silence

oneLiner: 白天时间都被别人占了，就用熬夜「夺回」一点自己的时间——明知该睡却舍不得睡。
oneLinerEn: When the day's hours belong to others, people stay up late to reclaim a little time for themselves—knowing they should sleep yet loath to give it up.
detail: 白天被工作、课业与责任填满，一到夜里终于有一段「说了算」的时间，于是刷手机、追剧、发呆，用牺牲睡眠换回一点自主与愉悦。研究把它和「自我调节资源被白天耗尽」相连：越是白天控制感低、自由时间少的人，越容易用它补偿。代价是睡眠债与次日的注意力、情绪进一步受损，形成恶性循环。破局不在意志力硬扛，而在白天预先切出一点真正属于自己的留白，让夜晚不必靠透支来讨还。
detailEn: Filled by work, study and duty by day, one finally owns a stretch of time at night—so people scroll, binge and zone out, trading sleep for a scrap of autonomy and pleasure. Research links it to self-regulation depleted across the day: the lower the daytime sense of control and the less free time, the more one compensates. The cost is sleep debt that further damages next-day attention and mood, a vicious cycle. The way out isn't white-knuckle willpower but carving out a little genuine margin in the day, so the night needn't be overdrawn to pay it back.

sources.label: Kroese et al. (2014), Bedtime Procrastination

oneLiner: 我们对一段经历的回忆，只由「最强烈的一刻」和「结束时」决定，而非全程的平均。
oneLinerEn: We remember an experience by its most intense moment and how it ended—not by its average across time.
detail: 卡尼曼的结肠镜实验：让一组病人接受更长、但结尾更轻的检查，他们事后回忆的痛苦反而更低，也更愿复查。「时长」被记忆忽略，评价被高峰与终点两处锚定。启示：一次旅行的收尾、一场对话的最后一句，往往盖过了整段过程；给体验「设计结尾」，比压低全程均值更能影响被记住的满意度。
detailEn: Kahneman's colonoscopy study: patients given a longer exam that ended gently recalled less pain afterward and were more willing to repeat it. Duration is dropped by memory, which anchors its verdict on the peak and the end. The lesson: how a trip closes or the last line of a conversation often overshadows the whole run—designing an ending shapes remembered satisfaction more than lowering the average.

sources.label: Kahneman et al. (1993)

oneLiner: 当挑战与技能刚好匹配，人会全神贯注、忘却时间——这就是心流。
oneLinerEn: When challenge and skill match just right, you become utterly absorbed and lose track of time—that is flow.
detail: 契克森米哈赖提出：任务太难则焦虑、太易则无聊，唯有「跳一跳够得着」才进入忘我的投入，行动与意识合一、自我批评暂停。它需要清晰目标、即时反馈与专注的环境。与「拖延」相反，心流中的人不靠外部奖励，活动本身就是回报。它常被简化成「努力就会快乐」的口号，其实对触发条件颇为挑剔。
detailEn: Csikszentmihalyi's idea: too hard breeds anxiety, too easy boredom; only a stretch just beyond skill triggers absorbed, self-forgetting engagement, action merging with awareness and the inner critic pausing. It needs clear goals, instant feedback and an undistracted setting. The opposite of procrastination, the person in flow isn't driven by reward—the activity is its own return. Often flattened into 'effort brings joy', it is in fact picky about its conditions.

sources.label: Csikszentmihalyi, Flow (1990)

oneLiner: 「如果到了某情境，我就做某事」的预案，把意志力消耗降为自动触发。
oneLinerEn: An 'if this situation arises, then I do that' plan turns effortful willpower into an automatic cue.
detail: 光有目标（「我要多运动」）多半落空。戈尔维策发现，把目标翻译成具体的「何时、何地、如何做」的条件计划，成功率成倍上升。它预先在脑中「排练」线索，届时情境像开关一样直接唤起行为，无需临场挣扎——是「下决心」与「真做到」之间那座被低估的桥。
detailEn: A bare goal ('exercise more') usually fizzles. Gollwitzer found that translating it into a concrete when/where/how 'if–then' plan multiplies success. It pre-rehearses the cue so the situation later flips a switch and the act runs off with no on-the-spot struggle—the underrated bridge between resolving and actually doing.

sources.label: Gollwitzer (1999)

oneLiner: 总怕别人正经历比自己更好的事，于是放不下手机与通知。
oneLinerEn: A persistent dread that others are having richer experiences than you—so you can't let go of the feed.
detail: 它滋生在社交媒体上被精心剪辑的「他人现场」：刷屏尽是别人的高光，拿来对照自己未经修饰的日常。它与更低的生活满意度、更差的睡眠、更强的刷屏强迫相关（无脑下滑、报复性熬夜都是它的近亲）。解毒剂未必是「戒网」本身，而是识破那份「比较的错觉」——被展示的生活，从来不是完整的生活。
detailEn: It grows on social media's curated 'live feeds' of others—endless highlights set against your own unedited ordinary days. It tracks with lower life satisfaction, poorer sleep and compulsive checking (mindless scrolling and revenge bedtime are its kin). The antidote is not quitting the phone per se but seeing through the comparison: the life on display was never the whole life.

sources.label: Przybylski et al. (2013)

oneLiner: 跌倒时像对待好友那样善待自己，而非鞭笞——它比自我批评更能让人重新站起。
oneLinerEn: Treating yourself like a good friend after a fall, rather than whipping yourself—this lifts people back up better than self-criticism.
detail: 为什么：许多人不把失败当人之常情，而当作自己「不行」的证据，越苛责越泄气。怎么办：三重自我关怀——正念地承认「这确实难受」、提醒自己「人人都会如此」、对自己说一句宽慰的话。研究表明，它降低焦虑、增强坚持，比一味追高自尊更稳。
detailEn: Why: many read failure not as part of being human but as proof they are 'no good', and the harsher the self-blame the more they stall. What helps: three notes of self-compassion—mindfully admit 'this hurts', recall 'everyone fails', and offer yourself a kind word. Research finds it lowers anxiety and steadies persistence, more reliably than chasing high self-esteem.

sources.label: 内夫《自我关怀的力量》
sources.labelEn: Neff, Self-Compassion

term: 自证预言（皮格马利翁效应）
oneLiner: 对他人的期待会悄悄改变他的表现：被看好者真的更出色，被看低者逐渐坠落。
oneLinerEn: Expectations quietly change performance: the favored truly rise, the doubted gradually fall.
detail: 机制：老师被告知某些孩子「潜力大」（实为随机抽取），便不自觉地多给关注、耐心与机会，孩子果然进步更快。循环是——你的期待，塑造你的对待，改变他的表现，再印证你的期待。启示：对他人（尤其孩子）多怀成长式的高期待，同时警惕负面标签的自我实现。
detailEn: Mechanism: told certain children were 'bloomers' (randomly picked), teachers unwittingly gave more attention, patience and chance—and those kids did gain more. The loop: your expectation shapes your treatment, changes his performance, then confirms your expectation. Takeaway: hold growth-minded high expectations of others (especially children), and beware the self-trap of negative labels.

sources.label: 罗森塔尔与雅各布森《课堂中的皮格马利翁》
sources.labelEn: Rosenthal & Jacobson, Pygmalion in the Classroom

oneLiner: 不必跑马拉松，哪怕快走二三十分钟，也能实打实地减轻焦虑、抬升心情。
oneLinerEn: No marathon needed—a brisk 20–30 minute walk reliably eases anxiety and lifts mood.
detail: 为什么：运动会释放内啡肽与内源大麻素，带来「跑者愉悦」；它同时降低压力激素、改善睡眠，并给出「我在照顾自己」的自我效能证据。对轻中度抑郁，规律有氧的效果在多项研究中可与部分治疗手段相当。怎么办：选喜欢的、能坚持的形式，「动起来」比「练多狠」更重要。
detailEn: Why: exercise releases endorphins and endocannabinoids (the 'runner's high'), while lowering stress hormones, improving sleep and giving evidence of 'I care for myself'—self-efficacy. For mild-to-moderate depression, regular aerobic work in many studies rivals some treatments. What helps: pick a form you enjoy and can keep; 'moving' matters more than 'how hard'.

sources.label: 《英国运动医学杂志》伞状综述
sources.labelEn: BMJ Open Sport & Exercise Medicine umbrella review

term: 「默认选项」如何替我们做决定
oneLiner: 预选好的选项，大多数人懒得改——一个小小的默认值，就能左右器官捐献与养老金。
oneLinerEn: Pre-set options most won't bother to change—a tiny default can steer organ donation and pensions.
detail: 为什么：默认自带「推荐」的暗示，又省去决策成本；在复杂或陌生的选择面前，人倾向于随大流、维持现状。应用：把想推广的行为设为默认（如养老金自动加入、节能选项），效果远胜事后劝说。但也正因它强大，用得好是助推、滥用则是操纵，须警惕「暗桩」式默认。
detailEn: Why: a default reads as a recommendation and saves the cost of deciding; before complex or unfamiliar choices people tend to stay put. Use: make the behavior you want the default (auto-enrolling pensions, energy-saving settings)—far stronger than after-the-fact persuasion. But precisely because it is powerful, well-used it nudges and abused it manipulates—beware 'dark-pattern' defaults.

sources.label: 约翰逊与戈德斯坦《默认的力量》
sources.labelEn: Johnson & Goldstein, Defaults and Decision Outcomes

termEn: How to Say No Without Burning the Bridge
oneLiner: 让人受伤往往不是「不」本身，而是被否定感——立场、真实难处、替代方案，三样齐了才叫一次干净的拒绝。
oneLinerEn: What stings is rarely the 'no' itself but the feeling of being dismissed—stance, honest constraint and an alternative make a refusal survivable.
detail: 为什么难：拒绝在开口之前就被放大了。聚光灯效应让我们高估对方会记住多少、也高估自己那份尴尬，于是先答应、再拖延、最后怨恨——把一次小成本变成这段关系的长期负债。怎么做：三段式。先给明确立场（这次不行），不含糊、也不留假希望；再给真实难处而不是借口，借口一旦被拆穿，赔进去的是信用；最后给替代——换个时间、换个方式，或者引荐更合适的人。核心是把「你不行」换成「这件事我做不到」：拒绝的是请求，不是人。边界：拖延不如早说，对方越晚知道越难重新安排。还有一条常被忽略——一贯有求必应的人，第一次说不反弹最大；而有原则的人偶尔说不几乎无损。所以保护你的不是每次都答应，而是可预期的诚实。
detailEn: Why it is hard: a refusal is inflated before it is spoken. The spotlight effect makes us overestimate how much the other person will remember and how awkward we look, so we agree, stall, then resent—turning one small cost into a long-term liability on the relationship. How: three moves. State the position plainly (not this time) without leaving false hope; offer a real constraint rather than an excuse, since an exposed excuse costs credibility; then supply an alternative—another time, another form, or someone better placed. The core is swapping 'you are too much' for 'I cannot do this thing': refuse the request, not the person. Caveat: say it early, because the later people learn, the harder it is for them to rearrange. And those who always comply pay the most for their first no, while people with visible principles pay almost nothing—what protects you is not compliance but predictably honest limits.

sources.label: 吉洛维奇等《社会判断中的聚光灯效应》
sources.labelEn: Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky, The Spotlight Effect in Social Judgment

termEn: Gifts, Cash and the Debt of Reciprocity
oneLiner: 礼物从不免费：收下的那一刻就欠下一笔没有到期日的债——互惠既是纽带，也是杠杆。
oneLinerEn: A gift is never free: accepting it opens a debt with no due date—reciprocity bonds people and levers them.
detail: 机制：格尔纳把「互惠规范」列为社会结构的支柱之一——人接受了好处就会产生应当回报的不适，而且回报往往超额、延后。随份子、年货、请客走的就是这条通道：金额被记住、被比较、被转述，一个人在关系网里的余额，决定他临时开口时能借到什么。怎么用得干净：一是把赠予说成赠予，别让它变成预付的控制——「我帮你带过孩子」是把债当场拿出来讨；二是接受时把回报的方式与时限说清，含糊的亏欠最容易发酵成怨恨；三是警惕以礼物开局的请求，得寸进尺效应说明先应下小恩惠，之后就更难拒绝大要求。边界：关系越近，越不该精确对账。把人情算成账目，往往正是它开始破裂的信号。
detailEn: Mechanism: Gouldner listed the norm of reciprocity among the pillars of social structure—once we take a benefit we feel obliged to return it, and the return tends to be larger and later. Wedding cash gifts, New Year provisions and hosted meals all run on this channel: amounts are remembered, compared and retold, and a person's balance in a network decides what they can borrow when they ask in a hurry. How to keep it clean: call a gift a gift rather than prepaid leverage—'I minded your kids once' is a debt collected on the spot; when accepting, name the form and timing of the return, since vague owing ferments into resentment; and distrust requests that open with a present, because foot-in-door shows that a small accepted favour makes the large one harder to refuse. Boundary: the closer the relationship, the less exact the accounting. Keeping score is usually the symptom that the bond has already begun to fail.

oneLiner: 「改天请你吃饭」不是日程而是关系的标点——高语境里，礼貌语传递的是距离与善意，不是信息。
oneLinerEn: 'Let's eat out sometime' is punctuation, not a schedule: in high-context talk politeness carries distance and goodwill, not information.
detail: 为什么会有客套：语言不只报告事实，也维护面子。汉语里的「您」「麻烦您」「不太合适」承担缓冲功能，把直接否定包起来，让对方有台阶、让场面不塌。霍尔把这类沟通称为高语境——大量含义放在关系、场合与措辞里，而不是字面上。怎么解码：看具体度，「改天聚」是礼节，「周三晚上七点、我发定位」是打算；看谁把成本留给自己，客套话总说「我来麻烦你」；看重复度，一次是礼貌，反复主动才是意愿。反向注意：把客套当真会白等，把客套当假会伤人。习惯低语境的人常抱怨「不直说」不够坦诚，但直说并非更诚实，只是把成本从听者转给了说者——两种风格各有代价，看清对方在为什么付钱就够了。
detailEn: Why formulae exist: language does more than report facts, it protects face. Chinese honorifics and hedged refusals work as cushions, wrapping a direct no so the other side keeps a step down and the scene does not collapse. Hall called this high-context communication—much of the meaning sits in relationship, setting and phrasing rather than in the words. How to decode: check specificity, since 'sometime' is ritual while 'Wednesday seven, I'll send a pin' is intent; check who keeps the cost, because courtesy always volunteers oneself ('let me trouble you'); check repetition, since once is politeness and repeated initiative is willingness. The reverse caution: reading formulae literally wastes your waiting, reading them as false hurts someone. Low-context speakers often call indirectness dishonest, but bluntness is not more truthful—it merely shifts cost from listener to speaker. Both styles charge; notice who is paying.

oneLiner: 当众逼人认错，多半只换来抵抗——先把面子保住，人才有可能改。
oneLinerEn: Cornering someone in public buys resistance: secure the face first and correction becomes possible.
detail: 机制：戈夫曼把面子定义为「在互动中主张的那份正面自我形象」，一旦被公开质疑，人会本能启动防御——合理化、否认、反击。因为此刻承认错误的成本不只是这件事，而是整个人。所以纠偏的第一目标不是让对方看见真相，而是把真相的价格降到他付得起。怎么做：把「你错了」换成「有个情况想跟你核对」；提供不丢人的解释通道（时间太紧、信息不全、我当时没说清），对方就能顺着走下来；能私下讲就别当众讲；必要时给一个可以公开的动作——主动认错的人，往往是刚被递了台阶的人。边界：给台阶不等于替人担责，原则问题上含糊只会把成本推到下一次。它也会有一种失效场景：对方把退让读成心虚。那时需要的是清楚的立场加上清楚的尊重，而不是更软的措辞。
detailEn: Mechanism: Goffman defined face as the positive social value a person claims in interaction; once publicly challenged, defences fire automatically—rationalise, deny, counterattack—because admitting the error now costs not just the error but the whole self. So the first job of correction is not to show the truth but to price it low enough to afford. How: trade 'you're wrong' for 'there's something I'd like to check with you'; leave an unshaming explanation open (tight deadline, missing information, I explained it poorly) so they can step down it; say it privately when you can; and where useful, offer one public action—people who own a mistake in front of others are usually those just handed a way out. Boundary: a way out is not carrying their responsibility; vagueness on matters of principle only defers the bill. One failure mode: the retreat is read as weakness. Then what is needed is a clear position plus clear respect, not softer wording.

term: 一次有效的道歉缺什么
termEn: What an Effective Apology Is Missing
oneLiner: 「对不起行了吧」为什么让人更怒：只有情绪、没有承认具体后果与承诺改变的道歉，是在替自己解围。
oneLinerEn: Why 'sorry, okay?' angers further: an apology with feeling but no acknowledgement of harm and no promise of change is self-relief, not repair.
detail: 研究：刘易基等人把有效道歉拆成若干要素——陈述事实、承认造成的伤害、表达悔意、提出补偿、承诺不再犯，其中「承认具体后果」与「承诺改变」权重最高；只描述自己多难受（「我也一直很自责」）会把焦点从被伤害的人挪回道歉者身上。为什么难：道歉是一次自我降格，权力感越高的人越难开口——权力本身就让人更少采纳他人视角。而接受方要的通常不是忏悔表演，是「你明白你做了什么」，所以「如果让你不舒服了」这类条件句最伤人：它把责任推回对方的敏感。结构建议：一句话说清做了什么，一句话说清对方承受了什么，一句话说接下来怎么办，然后停下来等回应。别加「但是」，那是转折的开始，也是道歉的结束。
detailEn: Evidence: Lewicki and colleagues decomposed effective apologies into elements—state the act, acknowledge the harm, express regret, offer repair, promise change—with acknowledging specific consequences and promising change carrying the most weight; describing only how awful you feel moves the spotlight back onto the apologiser. Why it is hard: apologising is a self-demotion, and the more power someone feels the harder it gets, since power itself reduces perspective-taking. What receivers usually want is not a performance of remorse but 'you understand what you did'—which is why 'if this made you uncomfortable' cuts deepest: it hands responsibility back to their sensitivity. A workable shape: one sentence on what you did, one on what they carried, one on what happens next, then stop and let them answer. Do not append 'but'—it is where the reversal starts and the apology ends.

sources.label: 刘易基等《有效道歉的结构探索》
sources.labelEn: Lewicki, Polin & Lount, An Exploration of the Structure of Effective Apologies

oneLiner: 会开口是一种能力：把成本、时限和退路说清楚，别逼对方用「拒绝」来保护自己。
oneLinerEn: Asking well is a skill: name the cost, the deadline and the exit, so the other side need not defend itself with a refusal.
detail: 为什么不敢开口：求助暴露依赖，人怕被看低。但研究的方向相反——出丑效应显示适度暴露不完美反而更讨人喜欢；真正消耗关系的也不是请求本身，而是含糊的请求：对方既估不出要花多少，又不好推辞，只能拖着或者疏远。怎么提：一句话说清要什么、什么时候要、大概多少投入；给出一个体面的拒绝方式（这周不方便就直说，我另想办法），降低对方说不的成本；说明为什么找他，具体的理由远比泛泛恭维有效；事后把结果回过去，让人知道自己确实帮到了什么——沉默的回报最容易让下一次没人伸手。边界：别把关系当提款机。连续单向索取、只在需要时出现、拿交情公开施压，都会迅速把账户清零。
detailEn: Why we freeze: asking exposes dependence and we fear being seen as small. The evidence runs the other way—the pratfall effect shows a measured imperfection makes us likelier, not less; what actually drains a relationship is not the ask but a vague one, where the other side cannot price the effort and cannot refuse cleanly, so they stall or drift. How to ask: one sentence on what you need, when, and roughly what it costs; offer a dignified no ('if this week is bad, say so and I'll find another way') to lower the price of refusing; say why this person, since a specific reason beats flattery; and report back afterwards so they learn the help landed—silent returns are what make people stop lending. Boundary: never treat a relationship as an ATM. One-way taking, appearing only when needed, and pressing private closeness in public all empty the account fast.

sources.label: 阿伦森等《出丑效应：能力与失礼对吸引力的影响》
sources.labelEn: Aronson, Willerman & Ham, The Effect of Practical Elegance on Interpersonal Attractiveness

termEn: Seating, Titles and the Script of a Meal
oneLiner: 座次和称呼不是繁文缛节，而是一套低成本信号：告诉每个人「你在这里被怎样看待」。
oneLinerEn: Seating and forms of address are not ceremony for its own sake but cheap signals telling everyone how they are regarded here.
detail: 为什么需要仪式：戈夫曼把日常互动看作有脚本的仪式，人们靠微小的形式确认彼此的位置。主位、上菜顺序、先敬谁、叫「某总」「老师」还是直呼名字——这些都在替关系定价，省下了大量「我们到底是什么关系」的谈判。实用做法：进入陌生场合先观察再表现——看谁坐主位、谁先动筷、谁的话被接住；称谓宁可略正式，等对方主动降格；介绍时把低位者介绍给高位者（「王总，这是小李」），被介绍的一方起身；座位拿不准就问一句，问比坐错便宜得多。边界：仪式一旦变成表演，成本就高过收益。真正让人舒服的，是形式上的稳妥加上注意力上的真诚——手机屏幕朝下放在桌上，比敬酒词漂亮更有用。
detailEn: Why ritual is needed: Goffman read everyday interaction as scripted ceremony, with people confirming each other's place through tiny forms. The seat of honour, the order of serving, who is toasted first, whether someone is 'Director Wang', 'Teacher' or just a name—all of these price the relationship and spare everyone the negotiation of asking what it is. Practice: in an unfamiliar room observe before performing—who takes the head seat, who lifts chopsticks first, whose remark gets picked up; keep address slightly formal until the other side downgrades it; introduce the junior to the senior ('Director Wang, this is Li') and rise when you are introduced; when unsure of a seat, ask—asking is far cheaper than guessing. Boundary: once ritual becomes performance its cost exceeds its value. What people actually register is formal steadiness plus real attention: a phone face-down on the table beats a better toast.

sources.label: 戈夫曼《互动仪式》
sources.labelEn: Goffman, Interaction Rituals

termEn: Speaking Well of People Behind Their Backs
oneLiner: 当面夸是礼节，背后夸才被认为可信——好消息绕一圈传回来时，分量翻倍。
oneLinerEn: Praise to someone's face is etiquette; praise behind their back is believed—and doubles in weight once it travels.
detail: 机制：坏比好更强——负面信息与评价在判断中的权重普遍高于正面，所以背后的坏话杀伤极大，背后的好话收益也极大。听者还会做一个推论：你在我面前怎么说他，就会在别人面前怎么说我，于是这句话同时给说话人贴上了标签。为什么有效：它绕过了防御。当面夸奖常被打折接收（他有求于我、不过是客气），而转述的好评看不出动机，可信度更高；社会比较让人对来自同级的评价格外敏感，一句背后的肯定常常比十次当面赞美更被记住。怎么做：把肯定说具体——哪个判断、造成什么后果，别夸天赋；在当事人不在场、话题相关时自然带出；如果被转述回来，不必否认，也不必追加。边界：只有一种情况会反噬，就是被看出你在用好评换取站队。
detailEn: Mechanism: bad is stronger than good—negative information carries more weight in judgement than positive, which is why talk behind a back damages so efficiently and also why praise does the same in reverse. Listeners draw a second inference too: how you speak of them to others is how you speak of anyone, so the sentence labels the speaker as well. Why it lands: it bypasses defences. Praise to someone's face gets discounted (he wants something, it's just politeness), while reported praise shows no obvious motive and so is trusted; social comparison makes evaluations from peers especially salient, so one word behind a back often outlasts ten compliments to it. Practice: make the credit specific—which judgement, what it caused—rather than praising talent; let it out naturally when the person is absent and the topic is live; if it comes back to you, neither deny it nor pile on. Boundary: it only rebounds when people see you buying allegiance with good words.

sources.label: 鲍迈斯特等《坏与好同样强大》
sources.labelEn: Baumeister et al., Bad Is as Strong as Good in Twenty-Four Psychological Phenomena

termEn: Who Speaks First in a Silence
oneLiner: 我们高估被冷落的概率、低估攀谈之后的愉快——冷场常常不是没人想说话，是两个人都在等。
oneLinerEn: We overestimate rejection and underestimate the enjoyment that follows: a silence is often two people waiting.
detail: 机制：艾普利等人的现场实验让通勤者与陌生人攀谈，结果双方都远比事前预期愉快，而事前几乎每个人都预判自己会被冷落。两层原因在起作用：虚假共识让我们以为别人更想独处，行动者—观察者偏差则让我们把自己的紧张算作情境、把对方的沉默算作性格。为什么值得练：弱关系带来信息与情绪的双重收益，而多数社交遗憾并不是说错话，是根本没开始。开场不必聪明：就地取材（共同处境）、具体而轻（问一个问题而不是给一个评价）、留出退路（对方答得短就收住）。注意：搭话不构成打扰的前提，是对方能轻易离开——车厢、排队、电梯适合轻聊；戴着耳机、看书、手上有明确事务时，沉默才是礼貌。把「不想聊」读成「没教养」，正是社交焦虑者最常见的误读。
detailEn: Mechanism: Epley and Schroeder's field experiments had commuters strike up conversation with strangers; both parties enjoyed it far more than predicted, yet beforehand nearly everyone expected to be rebuffed. Two biases explain the gap: false consensus makes us assume others want to be left alone, while the actor-observer split files our own nervousness as circumstance and their silence as character. Why practise it: weak ties pay in information and in mood, and most social regret is not a wrong sentence but a non-start. Openings need not be clever—use the shared situation, ask one concrete light question rather than offer an appraisal, and leave an exit (if the answer is short, close warmly). Note: cold-approach is only rude when the other person cannot leave—trains, queues and lifts suit light talk; headphones, a book or an obvious task mean silence is the polite option. Reading 'not today' as 'ill-mannered' is the most common misjudgement of the socially anxious.

sources.label: 艾普利《他心通：看见他人内心的科学》
sources.labelEn: Epley, Mindsight: The New Science of Seeing Others

oneLiner: 让人崩掉的很少是内容，多是「我这个人被否定了」的感觉——先对齐目标，再谈行为，最后谈影响。
oneLinerEn: Rarely the content detonates someone; it is the sense of being written off. Align on the goal, then behaviour, then impact.
detail: 为什么总谈崩：斯通与希恩指出，每句批评里都叠着三层对话——事情到底是什么（真相对话）、情绪怎么处理（情绪对话）、我算老几（身份对话）。冲突多发生在第三层：对方听到的是「你不行」，于是先自保，内容根本没进去。怎么说：先确认共同目标（我们要的都是这次别返工）；把评价换成可观察的行为与时间（这版数据有三处对不上，就在周三那封邮件里）；说影响而不是动机（客户会以为我们没核对，优于你太不负责）；最后把选择权交回去（你觉得怎么改，需要我给什么）。被批评的一侧同样有技巧：把「你错了」听成「这里有条信息」，先复述再回应，问一句「你希望我先改哪一件」，能立刻把情绪对话拉回真相对话。边界：否定密度过高会失效，连续批评让人关闭注意；峰终定律说明收尾那句被记得最久，所以结尾要停在下一步，而不是停在错误上。
detailEn: Why it blows up: Stone and Heen show that every piece of feedback stacks three conversations—what actually happened (truth), how we each feel about it (relationship), and who I am in light of it (identity). Conflict usually erupts in the third: the receiver hears 'you are inadequate' and defends, so the content never lands. How to say it: fix the shared goal first (we both want no rework this time); replace the verdict with observable behaviour and a timestamp (three figures in this draft don't match the Wednesday email); describe impact rather than motive (the client will read it as unchecked, not you are careless); then hand back the choice (how would you fix it, what do you need from me). Receiving has a technique too: hear 'you're wrong' as 'there is information here', restate before answering, and ask which single thing to change first—instantly pulling the emotional conversation back to the factual one. Boundary: a high density of negatives stops working, since consecutive criticism shuts attention down; the peak-end rule means the last sentence is what sticks, so end on the next step, not on the mistake.

sources.labelEn: Stone & Heen, Thanks for the Feedback

term: 四种带法，先看清自己是哪一种
termEn: Which of the Four Styles Are You
oneLiner: 把「管得多不多」和「接不接得住」分成两把尺，四个格子立刻能认出自己家像哪一格。
oneLinerEn: Split 'how much control' and 'how much warmth' into two rulers, and you can find your own cell in four.
detail: 两把尺：要求（有没有清楚的底线与期待）与回应（够不够温暖、愿不愿听孩子的话）。两高是权威型：规则明白，也允许孩子问「为什么」并得到回答；高要求低回应是专制型：「没有理由，因为我说的」；低要求高回应是纵容型：情绪全接住，却很少立规矩；两低是忽视型：既不要求也少回应，最常见于大人被工作、疾病或婚姻拖住的时候，而不是不爱。自查有用的地方在于：同一句「十点必须上床」落在不同格子里，孩子的解读完全不同——权威型里被读成关心，专制型里被读成控制，于是同样的规则换来完全不同的对抗强度。也要说清这套框架的局限：鲍姆林德的原始样本是上世纪六十年代以白人、中等收入以上的家庭为主；后续跨族群与跨阶层的重复里，权威型的优势稳，专制型的负面却弱得多（Chao 指出中文语境里「管教」本身就被孩子读成爱的表达）；权威型孩子成绩更好，一部分靠的是父母的时间与经济资源（Lareau 称为「协同培养」），不是态度自带魔法。所以自查不是为了给自己贴一个及格标签，而是找出可以调的那一格——多数人真正能加的是回应，而不是再叠一层要求。
detailEn: Two rulers: demandingness (are there clear limits and expectations) and responsiveness (how much warmth, how much listening). High on both is the authoritative style: rules are explicit and the child may ask why and gets an answer. High demand, low warmth is authoritarian: 'no reason, because I said so.' Low demand, high warmth is permissive: every feeling is received, few limits are set. Low on both is uninvolved, which usually shows up when a parent is swamped by work, illness or a marriage, not when they do not care. The audit pays off because the same sentence—'lights out at ten'—is decoded differently in each cell: as care in one, as control in the next, so identical rules buy wildly different resistance. The caveats belong in the ledger too. Baumrind's original sample was white, mostly middle-income families in the 1960s; in later replications across ethnic and income groups the advantage of the authoritative style holds while the harm attached to the authoritarian one fades (Chao notes that in Chinese contexts 'discipline' is itself read by children as love, so the label bundles high demand with low warmth and misreads such homes). And authoritative kids' better grades run partly through parental time and money—what Lareau calls concerted cultivation—not through attitude alone. So the point of the audit is not a passing sticker but the one dial you can actually turn, which for most parents is warmth, not another layer of demand.

term: 手想伸出去时，先等十秒
termEn: Ten Seconds Before You Step In
oneLiner: 代劳的冲动多半是大人的焦虑在动，不是孩子真的需要救援。
oneLinerEn: The urge to take over is usually adult anxiety moving, not a child who actually needs rescuing.
detail: 「直升机」一词来自青少年来访者的抱怨（1969 年吉诺特的书里，孩子形容母亲「像直升机一样在我头顶盘旋」），2000 年代后被用来命名一类持续监控、随时接管的养育；同一逻辑往前推一步就是扫雪机父母：孩子还没碰到障碍，先替他在前面铲平。它被批评的机制不是「管得严」，而是心理控制与机会剥夺（见「行为控制与心理控制」条）：孩子练不出自己判断风险、自己收尾、自己开口求助的能力，也拿不到「这事是我做成的」那条内部凭据；被高度接管的大学生更低自主、更依赖外部确认，而学业表现并没有因此更好。可操作的五步：①事前把事分三档——安全与底线（立刻介入）、能力可及（先不介入）、偏好（穿什么、先写哪一科，归他自己定）；②设一个十秒延迟，孩子卡住时先在心里数到十，多数时候他自己接上了；③把帮忙改成「陪而不代」：问「你打算怎么办，要我帮哪一步」，只补那一步，不接手整件；④事后复盘只问两句——哪一步是你自己完成的、下次想改哪里，不追加训话，第三句就把复盘变成审判；⑤焦虑归自己：给自己找出口（运动、与配偶分工、自己的朋友），不要在孩子身上取平静。边界：真正需要外部结构的孩子（发育、注意力或情绪方面的困难）需要的是更多提示而不是更少；撤退要按能力分步走，不是一次断掉；「放手不管」和「不回应」是两件事，后者才是有害的那一件。
detailEn: The word comes from an adolescent's complaint—in Ginott's 1969 book a teenager described his mother as 'like a helicopter circling over me'—and from the 2000s it named a style of constant monitoring and standby rescue. Push the same logic one step earlier and you get snowplow parenting: the obstacle is cleared before the child ever reaches it. What researchers object to is not strictness but psychological control plus confiscated practice (see the entry on behavioral versus psychological control): the child never gets to rehearse judging risk, finishing a task, or asking for help, so they also never gain the internal evidence that 'I did that'. Highly scaffolded college students show lower autonomy and more reliance on outside validation, without better academic performance. Five workable steps: sort events in advance into safety and non-negotiables (step in now), skills within reach (hold back), and preferences (what to wear, which subject first—his call); impose a ten-second delay when he stalls, and most of the time he picks the thread back up; convert help into company by asking 'what is your plan, which part do you want me for' and supply only that part; debrief with two questions only—which part did you finish yourself, what would you change next time—because a third turns review into a verdict; keep your own anxiety in your own lane (exercise, a split with your partner, your own friends) rather than harvesting calm from him. Boundaries: children who genuinely need external structure—developmental, attentional or emotional difficulties—need more prompts, not fewer, and withdrawal should be stepped to match competence, not cut at once. And 'hands off' is not 'no response'; the second is the harmful one.

term: 孩子不肯说的时候，先别急着问
oneLiner: 追问是压力，复述是邀请：把「今天怎么样」换成「你刚才那句听起来挺烦」。
oneLinerEn: Questioning presses, echoing invites: swap 'how was today' for 'that sounded irritating'.
detail: 为什么越问越沉默：孩子在报告坏消息之前会先估对方的反应，一估就是「说了要被讲道理」，于是选择闭嘴；提问密度高、每个回答后面紧跟建议，等于把对话变成审讯。三条替代路。第一条是积极倾听（戈登的 P.E.T.）：不评价地把话里的情绪当信息返回去——「数学课上被点名，你觉得难堪」；规矩是只回到他给的料，不添他自己没说的情节，说错了他会纠正你，那也算开口。第二条是「我信息」（同一本书里的另一个工具）：把「你怎么又……」换成三段——可观察的行为、对我的具体影响、我的感受（「看到书包扔在楼梯上，我搬上去容易踩着，我有点烦」）；少了影响那一段会被读成规则宣告，加了形容词（「你太不负责」）就退回指责。顺序值得记：先确认情绪，再谈事情——情绪没被接住时内容进不去，这与成人反馈里的三层对话同理（见「批评怎么说才不炸」）。第三条留给不肯当面说的年纪：并排不对面——一起走路、洗碗、开车时视线分开，坦白率明显高于面对面审问；同时把「有事跟我说」这种空邀请换成具体的（「明天要面试，要不要先跟我说一遍，我听着」）。边界：沉默本身不是问题，长期退缩加上吃饭、睡觉、成绩一起掉，才是要找专业帮忙的信号；也别把倾听当侦察手段，孩子一旦发现共情是为了套话，门会关得更严。
detailEn: Why more questions yield less speech: before reporting bad news a child prices the reaction, and the price usually reads as 'I will get a lecture', so silence is the cheaper option; a high question rate with advice bolted onto every answer turns talk into interrogation. Three alternatives. First, active listening from Gordon's P.E.T.: hand the feeling back as information without verdict—'you were named out in front of the class, that felt humiliating'. The rule is to use only what he gave you; if you add a plot he did not say, he will spend his energy correcting you, which is also speech. Second, the I-message from the same book: replace 'you always...' with three parts—observable behavior, its concrete cost to me, my feeling ('the bag on the stairs, I trip carrying it up, I get annoyed'). Drop the cost and it reads as a rule announcement; add an adjective and it slides back into blame. Order matters: confirm the feeling before the facts, because content cannot land while the feeling is unreceived—the same three-layer problem as adult feedback. Third, for ages that refuse face-to-face confession: side by side beats eye to eye—walking, washing up, a car ride, where the gaze is unbolted, and disclosure rates rise; and swap the empty 'tell me if anything's wrong' for a concrete invitation ('say your interview out loud to me first, I will just listen'). Limits: silence is not the symptom—persistent withdrawal plus eating, sleeping and grades slipping together is when professional help belongs. And never use listening as reconnaissance: once a child finds that empathy is an extraction tool, the door shuts far tighter.

term: 孩子情绪炸开时，当教练别当法官
termEn: Coach the Storm, Do Not Judge It
oneLiner: 五步里最常被跳过的是第二步：把崩溃当成一次教学机会，而不是必须马上止住的失礼。
oneLinerEn: The step parents skip is the second: treat the meltdown as a teaching moment, not a breach of manners to stop at once.
detail: 戈特曼一家按家长对负面情绪的默认姿态分四种：不认可（情绪是坏毛病）、忽略（别当真，去吃点什么）、放任（只共情不设限）、情绪教练（先共情、再立界限、一起解决）。教练五步：①先觉察自己和孩子的情绪各到哪一格（心率差一级，能用的处理方式完全不同）；②把情绪时刻当作亲近与教学的机会，而不是麻烦；③先给共情、确认感受——感受没有对错，行为有；④帮孩子给情绪命名，一次只给一个词（这一步同时练情绪粒度，命名本身就能降低唤起，见「给情绪命名」条）；⑤立界限并一起想下一步：「你可以恨妹妹，但不能动手；下次想推的时候来找我」。证据要说清：情绪教练与儿童情绪能力的关联确实存在，但元分析给出的强度小于畅销书承诺的量级，而且多为相关设计——会做情绪教练的家庭本来就更多资源、更稳的作息，不能把相关读成因果。争议较少的是第四步与第五步各自有效：命名降唤起，清楚的界限与可预期的后果让情绪不至于失控（见强化与操作性条件）。两件事别搞反：接住情绪不等于同意行为；也不要要求「马上不哭」，那是在情绪上再叠一层羞耻，孩子学会的是把情绪藏起来而不是处理它。
detailEn: The Gottmans sorted parents by their default stance toward negative feeling: disapproving (feelings are bad habits), dismissing (do not take it seriously, have a snack), laissez-faire (all empathy, no limits), and emotion coaching (empathy first, limits next, solve together). The five coach steps: notice your own arousal and the child's, since one level apart changes what you can use; treat the feeling moment as intimacy plus teaching rather than an interruption; validate first—feelings carry no verdict, behavior does; help the child name it, one word at a time (this doubles as training in granularity, and labeling itself lowers arousal); then set the limit and plan the next move: 'you may hate your sister, you may not hit her; come find me next time the push builds'. Keep the evidence honest: coaching does correlate with better emotional competence, but meta-analyses put the effect well below what the popular books promise, and nearly all of it is correlational—families that coach also have more time and steadier routines, so the arrow is not settled. What is least contested is that steps four and five each work on their own: naming lowers arousal, clear limits plus predictable consequences stop feeling from escalating into action. Two inversions to avoid: receiving the feeling is not approving the behavior; and demanding 'stop crying right now' stacks shame on top of feeling, teaching the child to hide it rather than handle it.

termEn: Two Kids Fighting: Skip the Referee Whistle
oneLiner: 比较是他们之间最直接的通道——一句「你看弟弟」，比抢走玩具更能定下敌意。
oneLinerEn: Comparison is the fastest channel between siblings; one 'look at your brother' sets hostility deeper than the stolen toy.
detail: 机制有三层。第一，孩子之间的社会比较是自发运行的，父母把它正式化后成本剧增：研究里更能预测孩子适应的，不是父母实际是否偏心，而是孩子感知到的差别待遇——谁被允许更晚睡、谁被夸得更多、谁被叫去背锅。第二，同胞冲突的价值被低估：争执里练的是主张、讨价还价和读对方意图，邓恩与普洛明观察到同胞间的冲突与协商强度远高于同伴关系；若父母每次都裁决，这份练习就被抽走，孩子还多学到一条捷径——找大人。第三，他们争的往往不是那块饼干，而是「爸妈的那一份」能否被保住。怎么做：不裁谁对，改为描述规则与限制伤害（「家里的规矩是不动手；玩具归先拿到的人，你们要不要换个玩法」）；把孩子拉进解决（「你俩都想玩这辆车，今晚我们想三条办法，选一条你们都能过的」）；给年长者任务但不给身份（别要求「你是哥哥就得让」，那是把弟弟变成敌人）；单独相处的时间按人头排，而不是平分；表扬要具体、不跨人比较（「你刚才把轮子装上了」优于「你比妹妹聪明」）；和解也要教——怎么开口、怎么给对方台阶（见「给人台阶下」），多数孩子不是不想和，是不会和。另需分清：频率正常的打闹，与一方持续无力反抗、有隐藏性与伤害意图的欺凌不是一回事，后者要按欺凌处理而不是「孩子之间的问题」。
detailEn: Three layers. First, social comparison between siblings runs by itself; parents formalize it at terrible cost—what predicts children's adjustment better than whether parents actually favor one child is what the child perceives: who gets the later bedtime, who gets praised more, who is drafted as the scapegoat. Second, sibling conflict is undervalued: arguing is where claiming, bargaining and reading another's intent get practiced, and Dunn and Plomin found contention and negotiation far fiercer between siblings than among peers; every parental verdict removes that practice and adds a shortcut—run to an adult. Third, what is contested is rarely the biscuit but whether one's share of the parents is safe. What works: refuse to adjudicate who is right and describe the rule instead ('no hands in this house; the toy stays with whoever had it first—do you want a different arrangement'); pull them into the fix ('you both want the car; tonight we invent three options and pick one you can both live with'); give the elder tasks but not an identity—'you are the big brother, so yield' turns the younger one into an enemy; schedule one-on-one time per head rather than splitting it evenly; praise specifically and never across children ('you got the wheel on' beats 'you are cleverer than her'); and teach reconciliation, how to reopen and how to leave a step down, because most children want to make up and simply do not know how. One distinction to keep: ordinary scuffles at normal frequency are not bullying—where one side cannot fight back, it is hidden, and it is intended to harm, treat it as bullying, not as 'kids being kids'.

term: 老人帮带娃，分歧怎么谈
oneLiner: 三代同养最容易塌的不是溺爱，而是「谁是一把手」没有明说。
oneLinerEn: What collapses three-generation care is rarely indulgence; it is that nobody named who has the final say.
detail: 先把好处记在账上：稳定的第二依恋对象、父母的喘息、语言与节日的连续；孩子与祖辈亲厚本身就是韧性资源。塌的地方几乎都出在规则接口：①默示权限不明——父母以为自己是决策者，老人以为自己是执行者兼家长，孩子很快学会「找奶奶签」；②面子通道——当面指出老人的做法错了（「你这样喂会噎着」）在关系里被读成否定其付出，于是抵抗的不是知识而是位置；③补偿心理与体力限制——老人偏向有求必应与「别磕着」，于是一致性和边界在两头不一致；④分离风险——若幼年主要由祖辈带、父母只在晚上出现，孩子对「谁是主要依恋对象」会按事实而不是按名分来定，父母的权威得后期重新建立。可操作的解法：先做一份权限清单（安全、医疗、作息、屏幕、零花钱五格，明确哪格谁说了算、哪格可以不同但当面不拆台）；沟通顺序按先给功劳再上新证据（「您做的饭他最爱吃，医生说这个阶段盐再少一点，我们试试这么做」），把新做法挂在老人已有的付出上；不当着孩子争论规则（一旦拆台，规则就失效，孩子学到的是用关系绕过规则）；也给老人一份清单（他的时间、体力、社交与休息，别把帮助当无限供给）；父母仍要保住每天一段只属于亲子的高频小事，睡前那十几分钟最划算。若孩子长期与父母分离，要主动补链接而不是补偿购物：固定时间、可预见、能参与他真实的生活（作业、朋友、他的口头禅）才算陪伴。隔代不是问题，接口没谈才是。
detailEn: Credit the gains first: a second steady attachment figure, relief for the parents, continuity of language and festival; a close grandchild is itself a resilience resource. Where it breaks is almost always the rule interface. One, unstated authority: parents think they decide, grandparents think they execute and also parent, and the child learns to get the grandmother's signature. Two, the face channel: correcting an elder in front of them ('that way of feeding can choke him') is read in the relationship as denying the labour, so what resists is not the knowledge but the position. Three, compensation and stamina: elders lean toward yes-to-everything and do-not-scrape-the-knee, so consistency and limits differ by household corner. Four, separation risk: if grandparents raise the child through the early years and parents only appear in the evening, the child settles who the primary attachment figure is by fact rather than by title, and parental authority has to be rebuilt afterwards. The workable fix: draw one authority sheet—safety, medical, sleep, screens, pocket money—and mark who owns each box and which differences may stand as long as nobody undermines the rule in front of the child; sequence your messages as credit first, new evidence second ('he eats your cooking happily; the doctor wants less salt at this age, let us try it this way'), hanging the new practice on what the elder already gives; never debate the rule in the child's hearing, because once it is split, the rule dies and the child learns to route around rules through relationships; give the elder a sheet of their own (time, strength, social life, rest) so help is not treated as infinite supply; and keep a small daily passage that belongs only to parent and child—the last ten minutes before sleep is the cheapest bargain. Where the child has lived apart for years, rebuild connection rather than buying compensation: fixed hours, predictable, present in his real life (homework, friends, his catchwords) counts as company. Grandparent care is not the problem; the untalked interface is.

term: 孩子到了出格年纪，怎么谈朋友与风险
termEn: Talking About Friends and Risk at Fifteen
oneLiner: 硬禁交友切的是你的信息渠道；同伴在场放大的是他已经在意的事。
oneLinerEn: Banning a friend cuts your own line of information; a peer audience only amplifies what already matters to him.
detail: 先把两件事分开。同伴影响不等于坏影响：亲社会同伴能提高投入与助人水平，青少年对「同伴怎么看」的敏感本身是可用的动力（见「群体极化」与「青少年奖赏缺口」条）。真正抬高事故率的是一个具体组合：同伴在场 + 没有大人在场 + 时间压力 + 新鲜感强的场景——加德纳与斯坦伯格的实验里，仅仅旁边坐着同伴就显著提高了青少年的冒险选择与事故数，而成年人几乎不变。所以重心不该放在筛朋友，而应放在拆掉这个组合、补上临场能力。四条具体做法：①给拒绝脚本并练出来：青少年临场缺的是词汇不是道理——练一句身份式拒绝（「我从来不喝这个」）、一句推责式拒绝（「我妈会闻我车里的味道，她会知道」），比讲十次危害有用；②留一条便宜的退路：约定一个暗号（一条短信或一个表情就代表「来接我，当晚不问不训」，这就是 Code X 式约定的用意，代价是当晚的沉默要忍住）；③认识朋友的家长而不是朋友的名单：把监控换成社交接入，你有了背景与信源，他也少一层被审查感；④家里保一点可预测性：固定共处的时段与清楚的底线（菲斯等人的家庭作息综述显示，规律作息与更少的问题行为、更好的情绪调节相关），协商规则时让他在「怎么定」上有发言权，比在「要不要」上让步更稳（见自我决定论）。要避免的三件事：禁止某一个朋友（会激发心理反抗并把话题关掉，见「越被禁止，越想做」条）、把他与朋友的忠诚与你对他的忠诚对立、以及事后那句「我早说过」。
detailEn: Separate two things first. Peer influence is not bad influence: prosocial peers lift effort and helping, and adolescents' sensitivity to what peers think is usable fuel (see group polarization and the adolescent reward gap). What actually raises accident rates is a specific recipe—peers present, no adult present, time pressure, and a novel or exciting setting. In Gardner and Steinberg's driving task, merely having peers alongside sharply increased adolescents' risk taking and crashes while adults barely moved. So the work is not screening friends but dismantling the recipe and supplying in-the-moment skill. Four concrete moves. Give refusal scripts and rehearse them: what a teenager lacks on the spot is vocabulary, not arguments—practice an identity refusal ('I never drink that') and a blame-shift refusal ('my mother sniffs the car, she will know'), which beats ten lectures on harm. Keep a cheap exit: agree a code (one text or one emoji meaning 'come get me, no questions, no lecture tonight')—that is the point of the Code X arrangement, and its price is your silence that night. Know the friends' parents instead of the friends list: swap surveillance for social access, so you hold context and a source while he loses a layer of being audited. Keep some predictability at home: fixed shared hours and clear bottoms—reviews of family routines tie regularity to fewer behavior problems and better emotional regulation—and let him have a vote on how rules are set rather than conceding whether they exist. Three things to avoid: banning one named friend (it triggers reactance and closes the topic), setting his loyalty to friends against your loyalty to him, and the closing line 'I told you so'.

term: 当着孩子面吵，要不要收场
termEn: Arguing in Front of the Kids
oneLiner: 真正伤孩子的不是冲突发生，而是冲突没被看见解决，或者把孩子拉进来当武器。
oneLinerEn: What harms children is not that conflict happens but that its resolution is never seen—or that the child is drafted as a weapon.
detail: 直觉是「别让孩子看见吵架」，证据指向另一处：孩子对父母之间的张力极敏感，敏感到的不是音量而是「这件事后来怎么样了」。卡明斯与戴维斯的情绪安全框架：孩子把父母的冲突读作关于自身安全的信号，未解决的僵局或漫长的冷战会让注意力一直挂在父母的温度计上，学习与合作自然掉；格里奇与芬查姆的认知背景框架进一步指出，若孩子把冲突归因于自己（「是我不乖」）、觉得威胁大、又相信自己无力影响，最容易出现内化问题。所以要分清三种：建设性争执（有具体议题、音量可控、当着他面和好，或至少说明「我们在商量一件事，明天会有结果」）其实是冲突与修复的现场教材；破坏性争执（人身攻击、摔门、长期冷战）应尽量避开，且必须事后修复；把孩子当工具最伤——让他传话、评判谁对、逼他站队、或把争吵的理由说成「都怪你不听话」，等于把家庭治疗所说的三角化变成日常。若已经失控了，蹲下来按年龄说三句：「我们吵是因为在争一件事，不是因为你」；「刚才那么大声，会让人害怕，对不起」；「我们已经商量好了／我们打算这样解决」。修复这一步比不吵架更关键，也更便宜；孩子从中学到的是「冲突可以收场」，这比一个永远没有分歧的家庭更有用。
detailEn: Instinct says hide the fight; the evidence points elsewhere. Children track parental tension with great precision, and what they read is not volume but whether the matter later resolves. In Cummings and Davies' emotional-security framework a parental quarrel is processed as a signal about the child's own safety, so an unresolved impasse or a long cold war keeps attention parked on the parental thermometer, and learning and cooperation fall as a result. Grych and Fincham's cognitive-contextual account adds the specifics: children who attribute the conflict to themselves ('because I was bad'), appraise it as threatening, and believe they can influence nothing are the ones most prone to internalising trouble. So separate three cases. Constructive disagreement—a concrete issue, volume in check, repaired in front of them or at least narrated ('we are working on something and will have an answer tomorrow')—is live teaching about conflict and repair. Destructive conflict—personal attacks, doors slammed, weeks of silence—should be kept away from them, and repaired afterwards if it leaks. Drafting the child does the real damage: messenger, judge, conscripted ally, or being told the fight was caused by them, which turns what family therapy calls triangulation into a household habit. If you did lose it, crouch and give three age-sized sentences: we are arguing about one thing, not about you; that noise was scary, and I am sorry for that part; we have settled it, or here is how we plan to. The repair matters more than the clean record, and costs less: what a child learns is that conflict can close, which is more useful than a household that never disagrees.

termEn: Mix Problem Types in One Round
oneLiner: 混着练当下更磕绊，但考试要的那一步——「这题该用哪一招」——恰恰只在混题里被练到。
oneLinerEn: Mixed practice feels worse now, yet it trains the very move an exam demands: spotting which trick a problem needs.
detail: 按题型一批批刷时，「该用哪一招」是免费的：上一题已经告诉你这一类怎么解。考试不给这个提示。交错练习把不同题型混进一轮，逼你每题先做辨识与选择，于是当下错题变多、手感变差，延后测验与迁移到新题却更好。做法：复习排程按 A—B—C 混排而不是 AAAAA；每轮里插几道跨章混题；数学、几何与语言辨析最吃这一套。边界也别忽略：连基本步骤都没建立的新手先要少量分块练习，一上来就混只会挫败，常见安排是「先分后混」；收益最大的是需要选策略的材料，纯背词汇表提升有限。
detailEn: Blocked practice hands you the answer to 'which trick does this need' for free: the previous problem already told you the type. Exams do not. Interleaving different types in one round forces that identification step every time, so performance looks worse in the moment while delayed tests and transfer come out better. In practice: schedule A-B-C mixes rather than AAAAA, drop cross-chapter questions into each round; math, geometry and language discrimination benefit most. Two limits: beginners who have not built the basic steps first need some blocked practice, since pure mixing just defeats them—'block, then mix' is the usual arrangement; and the payoff is largest where choosing a strategy is the hard part, not in raw vocabulary memorization.

termEn: Retry Your Errors a Day Later
oneLiner: 错题本抄满答案还是会掉进同一个坑；最该重做的，是你当时很确信却答错的那几道。
oneLinerEn: Copying answers into an error log rarely sticks; the items worth redoing are the ones you got wrong with confidence.
detail: 超纠正效应说的是反直觉的一件事：你越自信地答错，看到正确答案时记得越牢——那份意外把注意力顶到最高。所以错题本里最值钱的不是难题，而是「我当时很确定」的题。做法：错题先只标记不抄答案；隔一到两天空着手重答一遍，再核对；单独列一栏「高置信错误」，考前专挑它们。三条边界：必须有正确反馈，否则把错答反复提取反而更结实；低置信的蒙错不必同等对待，先补概念；这一效应多在词表与课文里验证，推到长论证与写作时要留余地。
detailEn: The hypercorrection effect is counterintuitive: the more confident you were when wrong, the better the correction tends to stick—the surprise itself raises attention. So the valuable items in an error log are not the hard ones but the ones you were sure about. In practice: mark errors without copying the answer first; a day or two later, reanswer them blank, then check; keep a separate list of high-confidence errors and run it before the exam. Three limits: feedback is mandatory, since retrieving a wrong answer repeatedly just hardens it; low-confidence guesses do not deserve the same treatment—fix the concept first; and most evidence comes from word lists and short texts, so extending it to long arguments and writing should stay modest.

termEn: Ask What Each Step Rests On
oneLiner: 差生念「这步怎么算」，好学生念「这步凭什么成立」：把这行小字写出来，理解才有的查。
oneLinerEn: Weak students say how the step is computed; strong students say why it holds. Writing that line makes understanding checkable.
detail: 切基等人 1994 年录下学生解代数题时的自言自语：好的学生几乎每写一步都给自己解释这一步的依据，差的学生只跟着步骤走。把「自解释」当习惯训练出来，成绩明显往上。机制是把被动跟做变成主动补全因果链，顺手暴露断掉的那一环。做法：例题每一步旁写一行小字「凭什么」；读完一节先盲写「这一节是怎么走到结论的」；写不出的地方记下来再去问人。边界：已经熟练的人被要求逐步解释反而会变慢（专长逆转效应），到那个水平该把脚手架撤掉；材料得本身可解释，纯套路操练收益小；赶时间时至少对卡住的那一步解释。
detailEn: Chi and colleagues recorded students thinking aloud while solving algebra problems in 1994: the strong ones explained the warrant behind nearly every step, the weak ones just followed the procedure. Training self-explanation lifted results. The mechanism is turning passive following into actively completing the causal chain, which exposes exactly where the chain breaks. In practice: write one line beside each step of a worked example saying what it rests on; after a section, blank-write how it reaches its conclusion; keep what you cannot write for questions later. Limits: requiring step-by-step explanation from people who are already fluent slows them down (expertise reversal), so remove that scaffold at that point; material has to be explicable in the first place, and drills gain little; when pressed for time, explain at least the step where you stuck.

termEn: Attempt It Before You Are Taught
oneLiner: 没教就去做、甚至全错，反而让你听课时抓得更准：错的那次尝试本身就是钩子。
oneLinerEn: Attempting a problem before instruction—even failing it—sharpens what you take from the lesson that follows.
detail: 两条证据指向同一件事。先测后学：预先尝试即使答错，也让随后的学习记得更多，因为错误把注意力和问题空间都打开了。卡普尔的「有效失败」更极端：在正式教之前，让学生分组硬解几道没学过、注定解不好的复杂题，之后听讲、延后测验与概念题的成绩反而超过直接听课的组。做法：翻开新章节先做课后三题，不查答案；听课前五分钟写下你猜这节讲什么、这题大概会怎么解；听完对照「我猜的 vs 讲的」，把差距写下来。边界：一定要有讲评闭环，只裸做不给反馈收益明显缩水；得提前说清这是流程不是评分，否则挫败感把好处吃掉。
detailEn: Two lines of evidence point the same way. Pretesting: attempting items before instruction, even wrongly, improves what you later retain, because the attempt opens attention and the problem space. Kapur's productive failure goes further: before any instruction, groups wrestle with complex problems they have not been taught and cannot solve, and they later outperform peers who were taught directly, on immediate, delayed and conceptual tests. In practice: do three end-of-chapter problems before reading the chapter; spend five minutes before a lecture writing what you expect it to cover and how the problem might go; afterwards compare your guess with what was taught and note the gap. Limits: it needs a debrief loop—bare attempts without feedback lose most of the benefit; and say out loud that this is procedure, not grading, or frustration eats the gain.

oneLiner: 把「我差不多了」写成数字再打脸：高估的那部分，就是下轮该练的。
oneLinerEn: Turn 'I pretty much know it' into a number, then get corrected—the overestimate is next round's material.
detail: 复习完的信心多半来自流畅感：材料越读越顺，大脑把顺当作已经掌握，于是学习判断系统性偏高。校准的办法是把判断先变成可打脸的数字：合上材料，写下「我现在能默写几条」「这卷我能考多少」，再做一次自测，看差多少，把高估的内容排进下一轮提取练习。科里亚特的研究显示学习判断高度依赖表面线索，一旦把线索从「读得顺不顺」换成「能不能想起来」，判断立刻贴近实际。做法是三栏纸：预测、实测、差值。边界：预测本身不增进记忆，只有配上提取才有用；记一次不算校准，要连着记；对已经高度焦虑的人，每天打分数可能加压，改成隔天一次。
detailEn: Confidence after review mostly comes from fluency: material reads smoother each pass, the brain files smoothness as mastery, and judgments run systematically high. Calibrate by turning the judgment into a number you can be wrong about: close the book, write down how many items you can now list and what you would score, then self-test and compare, and schedule the overestimated parts for the next round of retrieval. Koriat's work shows learning judgments lean heavily on surface cues; swap the cue from 'does it read easily' to 'can I get it back' and the judgment snaps closer to reality. The tool is a three-column sheet: predicted, actual, gap. Limits: predicting alone adds no memory—it only helps paired with retrieval; one data point is not calibration, keep logging; and for someone already anxious, daily scoring can add pressure, so move it to every other day.

oneLiner: 讲不清的那一句就是没懂的那一句；卡壳不是失败，是免费的诊断。
oneLinerEn: The sentence you cannot say is the one you do not know; stalling is a free diagnostic.
detail: 两条证据：一是生成效应，自己产出的词句比读到的记得牢；二是解释深度错觉，让人画自行车链条、说清拉链怎么咬合，多数人都画不出来，尽管他们确信自己懂。合上材料、对一个想象中的外行出声讲两分钟，不许用行话，卡住的地方做记号——那里才是真没懂，回去只读那一段，再讲一遍。这套常被叫作「费曼式」，但要点不在名字，而在卡壳把漏洞暴露出来。边界：讲一遍不等于记住，仍要隔天再讲一次；对隐性技能（写作手感、游泳、球类）语言复述替代不了练习；想象听众容易自我放水，找人真听更准。
detailEn: Two findings back this. The generation effect: lines you produced yourself are remembered better than lines you read. The illusion of explanatory depth: ask people to draw a bicycle chain or say how a zipper engages, and most cannot, though they are sure they know it. Close the material, explain out loud for two minutes to an imagined layperson with no jargon allowed, mark every stall—that is the part you do not know—go back and read only that stretch, then explain again. The move is often sold as Feynman-style, but the value is not the name: stalling exposes the gap. Limits: one telling is not retention, so tell it again tomorrow; for tacit skill (writing feel, swimming, ball games) verbal recount cannot replace practice; and an imagined listener lets you off easy, so a real one is more accurate.

term: 情绪炸开时，先管身体再讲道理
termEn: Handle the Body Before the Argument
oneLiner: 心跳顶着嗓子眼时讲不通道理——先处理呼吸与现场，再处理事情。
oneLinerEn: When your heart is in your throat, no argument lands: deal with breath and scene first.
detail: 为什么：情绪一上来先是身体先动（心跳、呼吸、肌肉绷紧），前额叶重新拿回方向盘要几十秒到几分钟；在高峰期谈条件，几乎都会谈崩——这正是「冷热鸿沟」说的：冷静时的你猜不到激动时的你会怎么决定。怎么办：① 先离开现场，去接水、走到走廊，把话头推到「我们十分钟后再说」；② 把呼气拉长，试「循环叹息」：用鼻子吸气、再补一小口把肺填满、然后从口缓缓呼出，斯坦福 2023 年的随机对照里，每天五分钟连做四周的人积极情绪上升、静息呼吸频率下降，幅度优于同时长的正念观察呼吸；箱式呼吸也有效，各组之间的差别并不大。③ 若已恐慌到发麻，做「着陆」：说出眼前五样看得见的东西、四样摸得到的……限度：这类练习争取的是时间而不是结论，单次几分钟只压当下紧张；研究用的是健康人的自评量表，不能替代治疗；有呼吸系统疾病或憋气不适的人不要硬做。
detailEn: Why: when emotion hits, the body moves first—heart rate, breathing, muscle tension—while the prefrontal cortex needs seconds to minutes to take the wheel back. Negotiating at the peak almost always fails, which is exactly the hot-cold gap: calm you cannot predict agitated you. What to do: ① leave the scene, go get water or walk down the hall, and push the topic to 'let's pick this up in ten minutes'; ② lengthen the exhale with cyclic sighing—inhale through the nose, add a short second inhale to top the lungs up, then exhale slowly through the mouth. In Stanford's 2023 randomized comparison, five minutes a day for four weeks lifted positive mood and lowered resting breathing rate more than the same amount of watching the breath in mindfulness; box breathing worked too, and gaps between the breathing groups were small. ③ If panic has gone numb-and-tingly, run grounding: name five things you can see, four you can touch... Limits: these buys time, not conclusions—a single round blunts the moment only. The studies used self-report scales in healthy adults and are no substitute for treatment; skip breath-holding if you have respiratory trouble or it feels wrong.

term: 跟自己说话时，换个称呼
oneLiner: 把「我该怎么办」换成「小林，你打算怎么办」，焦虑往往先降一截。
oneLinerEn: Swap 'what should I do' for 'Xiao Lin, what are you going to do' and anxiety often drops a notch.
detail: 机制：密歇根的克罗斯（Ethan Kross）与其同事 2014 年的一组实验发现，临做有压力的即兴演讲、或回想一段痛苦经历时，用自己名字或「你」来跟自己对话的人，被客观评分者评为表现更好，事后报告的焦虑与反复咀嚼也更少；后续的脑电与成像工作显示这种「拉开距离」并不额外消耗认知控制资源——也就是说，它不是硬把情绪压住，而是不再只从「我」这个机位看事。怎么办：难受时换个口吻，用「给朋友提建议」的语气问自己：「你现在最难的是哪一块？下一步最小能动的是什么？」名字通常比「你」更稳，在心里默念就够。限度：证据主要来自实验室的演讲与回忆任务，长期的日常效果、以及部分人觉得「别扭」的体验都还没有大样本检验；换称呼不会替你把问题本身想清楚，它只是让你有力气去想。
detailEn: Mechanism: a set of 2014 experiments by Ethan Kross and colleagues at Michigan found that people who silently addressed themselves by name or with 'you'—right before a stressful impromptu speech, or while recalling a painful event—were rated as performing better by objective coders and reported less anxiety and less rumination afterwards; later EEG and imaging work suggested this self-distancing costs no extra cognitive control. In other words it is not white-knuckling the feeling down, it is stepping off the 'I' camera angle. What to do: when you are wound up, switch register and ask the way you would ask a friend—'what part is hardest right now, and what is the smallest thing you can move on?' A name usually works better than 'you', and muting it inward is enough. Limits: the evidence comes mostly from lab speeches and recall tasks; long-run everyday effects, and the awkwardness some people report, remain untested at scale. A new form of address will not think the problem through for you—it only gives you the room to.

sources.label: Kross et al. (2014), PLOS ONE

term: 把担忧圈进一天里的一小段
oneLiner: 担忧赶不走，但可以给它安排一个固定的到访时间。
oneLinerEn: You cannot chase worry away, but you can give it a fixed visiting hour.
detail: 机制：在广泛性焦虑里，担忧常被体验成「停不下来」，而越是压制越容易反弹——这正是白熊效应的日常版。行为疗法因此换了思路：不消灭担忧，而是给它设条件。博科维奇（Thomas Borkovec）等人 1983 年用「刺激控制」把担忧限定在每天固定的时间与地点，被试自我报告花在担忧上的比例和紧张感都明显下降；2023 年的元分析也支持它能减少日常担忧的时长与频率，但效应量小，且在确诊广泛性焦虑的人群中证据并不一致。怎么办：① 挑一个白天的 15—30 分钟，离睡前至少两小时，否则会把担忧搬进床前；② 别的时间冒出来，只写一句话记下，告诉自己「那个时段再想」；③ 到点先看清单，把条目分成「现在能动手的」与「想也没用的」，前者写下一步、后者放手；④ 闹钟一响就结束，不许续。核心不是拖延思考，而是让身体亲自验证一次：担忧并不危险，我可以决定什么时候回应它。
detailEn: Mechanism: in generalized anxiety, worry feels uncontrollable, and the harder you push it down the more it rebounds—the everyday version of the white-bear effect. Behavioural therapy changes the lever: not deleting worry but putting conditions on it. In 1983 Thomas Borkovec and colleagues used stimulus control to confine worry to one fixed time and place each day, and participants' self-reported share of time spent worrying, along with tension, dropped noticeably; a 2023 meta-analysis found small but reliable reductions in how long and how often people worry in daily life, while evidence in diagnosed GAD remains mixed. What to do: ① pick a 15-30 minute daytime slot, at least two hours before bed, or you will simply move the worry to your pillow; ② at other hours, write a single line to catch it and tell yourself 'that one waits for the slot'; ③ when the time comes, sort the list into 'I can act now' and 'reheating changes nothing'—write one step for the first, let the second go; ④ stop when the alarm rings, no extensions. The point is not to postpone thinking; it is to let your body check once that worry is not dangerous and you choose when to answer it.

term: 低到什么都不想做时，先把步子缩到最小
termEn: When Nothing Sounds Worth Doing, Shrink the Step
oneLiner: 不是等有劲了再做，而是先做一件小到不可能失败的事，劲才回来。
oneLinerEn: Don't wait for energy: do something too small to fail, and energy follows.
detail: 机制：低落有一个循环——提不起兴趣、于是更不动、生活里能带来回报的事更少、于是更没劲。「行为激活」正是拆这一环：雅各布森 1996 年把认知疗法拆开检验，发现去掉「改变想法」的成分，疗效并不下降；迪米姜 2006 年的随机试验里，在中重度抑郁患者中它与抗抑郁药相当。2023 年的元分析汇总成人门诊的效应量约 0.67，只保留低偏倚研究时降到 0.51，且参与者的脱落率略高，所以它有效但并非万能。怎么办：① 列几件过去给过你一点成就感或愉快感的小事；② 挑一件，写下具体时间与地点；③ 做完（哪怕做得很差）；④ 在活动前后各给心情打一次分，用记录代替「感觉没意思就不做」的判断。限度：这是治疗里的一个成分，自助方向可以参考，但不能替代正式治疗；如果低落加兴趣塌陷持续两周以上、影响睡眠食欲与学习交往，请告诉信任的大人或去专业渠道。
detailEn: Mechanism: low mood runs on a loop—nothing interests you, so you move less, so fewer rewarding things enter your life, so you feel flatter. Behavioural activation cuts exactly that link: Jacobson's 1996 component analysis found that removing the 'change your thinking' part did not reduce benefit, and Dimidjian's 2006 randomized trial found it comparable to antidepressant medication among moderately to severely depressed adults. A 2023 meta-analysis puts the pooled effect at about 0.67 for adult outpatient care, falling to 0.51 when only low-bias trials count, with a slightly higher dropout rate—real but not magic. What to do: ① list a few small things that once gave you a touch of mastery or pleasure; ② choose one and write down a concrete time and place; ③ do it, badly is fine; ④ rate your mood once before and once after, letting the record, not the 'it sounds pointless' feeling, decide. Limits: this is one ingredient of a treatment—self-directed use is a direction, not a substitute. If low mood with collapsed interest lasts beyond two weeks and starts eating sleep, appetite or study, tell a trusted adult or reach a professional channel.

sources.label: Dimidjian et al. (2006), Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
Cuijpers et al. (2023), Psychotherapy Research

term: 看材料之前，先把打分规则定下来
termEn: Set the Rubric Before You Read
oneLiner: 先定标准再看信息，人才不至于一路替心头好找理由。
oneLinerEn: Fix the standard before the material, or you will spend the reading defending your crush.
detail: 为什么：卡尼曼、西博尼与桑斯坦 2021 年指出，判断出错有另一半来自「噪声」——同样的材料，换个人、换个时间，结果散得离谱。而一旦先被某个选项打动，之后的阅读就自动变成替它辩护，这和确认偏误走的是同一条路。怎么办：① 把「这事行不行」拆成三五个互不代替的维度（成本、时间、可逆性、最坏情况、谁承担）；② 在看具体方案之前，先给每个维度写下权重与打分口径；③ 逐项独立打分，全打完了再形成整体印象，别边看边下结论；④ 有其他人参与时，先各自独立评完再开讨论，否则第一个发言的人就成了锚。限度：结构化会牺牲灵活性，面对真正前所未见的问题，规则本身可能就是错的；这套做法压的是随机波动，并不能替你确定哪条标准重要。
detailEn: Why: Kahneman, Sibony and Sunstein (2021) argue that the other half of judgment error is noise—the same file scored wildly differently by another person, or by the same person on another afternoon. And once a option wins you over early, every page after it turns into its defence lawyer, the same road confirmation bias takes. What to do: ① split 'is this good' into three to five non-substitutable dimensions—cost, time, reversibility, worst case, who carries it; ② write weights and scoring anchors for each before you look at any specific proposal; ③ score item by item independently and only assemble an overall impression at the end, instead of concluding as you read; ④ if others are involved, everyone finishes their own scores before the discussion, or the first speaker becomes the anchor. Limits: structure trades away flexibility, and for genuinely unprecedented problems the rubric itself may be wrong; this discipline suppresses random scatter, it does not tell you which criteria deserve weight.

sources.label: Kahneman, Sibony & Sunstein (2021),《噪声》
sources.labelEn: Kahneman, Sibony & Sunstein (2021), Noise

term: 先问一句：同类的事平均怎么样
termEn: Ask What the Same Kind of Thing Usually Does
oneLiner: 把自己放进一组相似案例里看分布，比把计划写得更漂亮更能纠偏。
oneLinerEn: Watching how look-alike cases end corrects you better than polishing the plan.
detail: 为什么：卡尼曼与洛瓦洛 1993 年写下同一种怪象——企业做决策时谨慎，做预测时却大胆。他们让投资人先给同类项目的实际回报打个「公平分」，再评自己手上那个，结果细节了解得越多、乐观得越厉害：内部信息只会加固叙事。「外部视角」问的是另一件事：看起来像这样的局面，历史上通常怎么收场。怎么办：① 找一个参考类别（同类项目、同届考生、同规模创业），② 查真实分布——完成率、实际耗时、失败比例，不管当初预测写了什么；③ 再列出让你这一个不一样的具体理由；④ 估一个偏移量并回看：这个调整幅度，在这组案例自己的波动范围内吗？限度：参考类别常常难找，找到的还多是幸存者；对真正全新的领域，没有分布可查，也只能退回判断本身。
detailEn: Why: Kahneman and Lovallo (1993) named the mismatch—firms are timid when they commit and bold when they forecast. They had investors first rate what comparable projects actually returned, then their own: the more project detail someone knew, the more optimistic the forecast, because inside information only strengthens the story. The outside view asks a different question—how do situations that look like this usually end. What to do: ① pick a reference class (similar projects, the same cohort, businesses of this size); ② get the real distribution—completion rates, actual time spent, failure share—regardless of what forecasts once said; ③ then list the concrete features that make yours differ; ④ estimate how far to shift, and check whether that shift even sits inside the spread the class itself shows. Limits: reference classes are often hard to find, and the ones you find over-represent survivors; for genuinely new territory there is no distribution, and you fall back on judgment.

sources.label: Kahneman & Lovallo (1993), Management Science

term: 点头之前，先假设它已经砸了
oneLiner: 把「可能出什么问题」换成「它已经失败了，原因是什么」，异议才有出口。
oneLinerEn: Swap 'what could go wrong' for 'it has failed—why', and dissent finally gets an exit.
detail: 为什么：正常讨论里，没人愿意在计划阶段说丧气话，怕显得不忠诚、不配合；于是风险被集体沉默挡在门外——团体迷思正是这样发生的。认知心理学家加里·克莱恩（Gary Klein）2007 年在《哈佛商业评论》提出「事前验尸」，依据是米切尔、鲁索与彭宁顿 1989 年关于「前视回溯」的发现：当一件事被想象成已经发生，人们找出原因的能力明显提高（克莱恩文中称约三成）。怎么办：① 让相关人先读完计划；② 主持人宣布「现在是半年后，这个项目已经惨败」；③ 每人独立写五分钟「它是怎么死的」，专收平时不好意思讲的那些；④ 依次各念一条不重复的理由，汇总之后据此改计划。限度：这套做法没有大样本随机检验，「30%」是克莱恩文章的转述而非同行评议的实验结论；假设失败也可能让人编出并不存在的风险，主持人若不善于收拢，现场容易变成互相指责。
detailEn: Why: in ordinary discussion nobody wants to speak gloom during planning—it reads as disloyalty—so risks get screened out by collective silence, which is how groupthink operates. Gary Klein proposed the premortem in the Harvard Business Review in 2007, leaning on Mitchell, Russo and Pennington's 1989 finding on prospective hindsight: when an event is imagined as already having happened, people get markedly better at generating reasons for it (Klein's article cites about thirty percent). What to do: ① everyone reads the plan first; ② the facilitator announces 'it is six months from now and this project has failed spectacularly'; ③ each person writes alone for five minutes—how did it die—especially the objections usually left unsaid; ④ go around once, each stating a reason not yet heard, then revise the plan against the list. Limits: no large randomized test backs the procedure; the '30%' is a claim relayed in Klein's article, not a peer-reviewed effect, and a failure premise can also manufacture risks that do not exist. Without a steady facilitator the session turns into blame.

sources.label: Klein, Performing a Project Premortem (2007)
Mitchell, Russo & Pennington (1989), 前视回溯

term: 进去之前，先写下什么情况我就撤
termEn: Write Your Exit Line Before You Commit
oneLiner: 对付沉没成本，难的不是听懂道理，是没人提前替你画过撤退线。
oneLinerEn: Sunk costs are hard to beat not for lack of reason but for lack of a line drawn earlier.
detail: 为什么：已经花掉的会变成理由。阿克斯与布拉默 1985 年的经典实验里，剧院季票被随机按全价与两种折扣卖出，付得多的那场次来得更勤；滑雪度假的版本里，一半被试选了那个更贵却更不好玩、且钱都退不回来的周末——不是因为更好，而是因为「不去就更浪费」。「从现在看还值不值」这句问话道理上正确，可深夜和不甘心一起时很难生效，所以更实用的做法是把判断前移：还没投入时就写下退出条件——「如果三月底前没有第一个付费用户就停」「这门课到第六周还在拖我另外两件事，就退」——并把它交给一个会当真的时间或人。阿利利与韦滕布罗赫 2002 年发现，学生会自设带罚则的死线并因此做得更好，但自设的死线并不总落在最优位置，所以外部来盯比自我约定更牢。限度：撤退线本身可能被「再给一次机会」绕开，定线时把「谁有权改线、改线要付什么」一并写清。
detailEn: Why: what you already spent turns into a reason. In Arkes and Blumer's 1985 classic, theatre season tickets were sold at random—full price or two discounts—and those who paid more attended more shows; in the ski-trip version, half of the participants chose the dearer, less fun weekend although neither ticket was refundable. Not because it was better, but because skipping it would waste more. 'Is it still worth it from here' is correct in theory and weak at midnight, when resentment is loud. So move the judgment earlier: before you commit, write the exit condition—'stop if there is no first paying customer by the end of March', 'drop it if by week six it is still dragging down my other two'—and hand it to a time or a person who will hold you to it. Ariely and Wertenbroch (2002) found that students who set their own penalised deadlines performed better, but not at the optimal deadline, which is why an outside keeper beats a private vow. Limits: exit lines get routed around by 'one more chance'; write in advance who may move the line, and what moving it costs.

sources.label: Arkes & Blumer (1985), The Psychology of Sunk Cost
Ariely & Wertenbroch (2002), Psychological Science
